Police Border District Assistant Commander (Operations and Crime) Chief Superintendent Chan Kai-chak said that at 4:12pm today, police received a report that a local woman was found lying unconscious on the grass outside House 111, Ping Yeung Village. Police and ambulance personnel arrived at the scene and discovered the woman, with a roaming mongrel found beside her. Paramedics confirmed the woman was dead after examination.

Chan Kai-chak said the Border District Crime Unit had taken over the investigation. The scene was a licensed pet hotel and dog training centre that had been in operation since January this year, with no signs of burglary. Police reviewed closed-circuit television footage and found that at around 2pm, after the woman fed the mongrel on the outdoor grass, she attempted to return the dog to its cage, but the dog refused to enter and attacked her.

Police said CCTV footage ultimately showed the woman and the mongrel leaving the kennel and heading towards the grassy area. The deceased was a 33-year-old woman and the licensee of the pet hotel, and she was the only person working at the hotel at the time of the incident. The deceased sustained varying degrees of lacerations and animal bite wounds to her head, jaw, neck, and both arms. The mongrel involved is a one-year-old male, brought in by a dog volunteer for fostering on August 11 this year, in the hope of finding it an adopter. A forensic pathologist, representatives from the Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (SPCA), the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD), and the Labour Department assisted with the investigation at the scene. The mongrel will be taken away by the AFCD.

Police said they would investigate whether there were any violations or negligence. Police stated that the dog attacked while the woman was still alive, and both the woman and the dog had left the kennel and moved to the grassy area outside the kennel. The cause of death awaits confirmation by autopsy. The deceased was conscious at the time of the attack, and the attack by the mongrel lasted approximately one minute. The mongrel is approximately one metre long. Six other dogs were at the scene, all of which were inside dog cages at the time.
